A1.justification: Both are readable 47-page versions of the same paper, with matching main sections, algorithms, and appendices A–I. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable identification of the localized changes.

before.justification: v2 presents algorithms, theoretical regret guarantees, lower bounds, and proofs. Neither its main text nor appendices report original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical. Its main text and appendices contain no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: PABLO and its underlying algorithms are unchanged. Algorithm 3 retains the same parameter formulas, including c1 and c2; the revised constants occur in its proof.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or empirical evaluation. The theoretical coverage of static/dynamic regret and oblivious/adaptive comparators is unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline evaluations. The existing analytical comparisons with prior algorithms are unchanged.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols occur in either version, and no training or testing settings are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, sensitivity analyses, robustness tests, or error analyses. The existing illustrative discussions and auxiliary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. The high-probability guarantees are theoretical; the revisions concern proof constants rather than statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version, and the stated regret guarantees are unchanged. The numerical corrections affect an intermediate proof, assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3, Equation (13), now bounds 2Σ_T(w1:T), changes 3G to 6G and 16dG/24dG to 48dG, and explicitly identifies the per-learner terms used for cancellation. This is a localized correction to Theorem 4.4's proof; theorem statements, assumptions, and final regret rates are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 retain the same contributions: the PABLO reduction, comparator-adaptive guarantees, dynamic and high-probability regret bounds, and Euclidean-ball lower bound.

C2.justification: Interpretations of comparator adaptivity and path-length dependence, the limitations of the lower-bound arguments, and the future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, parameter specifications, and implementation explanations are retained. Updated equation references point to the same definitions; no code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, the reference list, and substantive positioning against earlier research are unchanged. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: Brief wording around the Appendix D.3 derivation is revised, equation cross-references are updated, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Section order and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation (13) is realigned to accommodate its explicit per-learner definition. One equation number is removed from the Appendix D.3.1 derivation, shifting subsequent numbering; other visual differences are small spacing adjustments. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Equation (13)'s corrected coefficients and explicit per-learner terms make the cancellation argument more consistent with the already specified c1 and c2. This improves local proof precision and readability, although the following page's reference to 2Σ_T(u1:T) remains unclear against the preceding Σ_T(u1:T) term. The algorithm and theorem statements are unchanged.
